speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your neck and arm pain, specifically noting any paresthesias or muscle weakness you are experiencing. To better assess the severity of your condition, could you tell me if your symptoms radiate to your fingers and which hand is affected?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your long-term diabetes and hypertension, could you tell me if you have a history of smoking, and do you experience any numbness in the "ring and middle fingers" specifically? Also, have you noticed any clumsiness with buttons or keys in your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with cervical spondylotic myelopathy.

The combination of progressive weakness, fasciculations, absent reflexes, and sensory changes in a patient with diabetes requires urgent neuroimaging and EMG. Please confirm if you have any difficulty breathing or swallowing, and REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI, Upper_Limb_Nerve_Conduction_Study.
